594: | Dixon (1970–74) made it exact | **Partly verified** [S5]: Dixon I (1970) defines momentum, spin and the centre of mass (`pβSαβ = 0`). Dixon II/III were **not opened**, and "made it exact" is not a quoted claim. |
595: | Thorne–Hartle 1985, *PRD* 31: surface integrals in a buffer zone | **Verified** [S8]: pp. 1815–1837; the paper's term is "buffer region". |
596: | Damour's "effacement" | **Verified** through Blanchet [S7]: the "effacing principle" (Damour 1983a, Les Houches proceedings, pp. 59–144). The 1987 chapter title is verified from a reference list; the chapter itself was not opened. |
597: | Control-volume momentum theorem (Lamb): force on a body = momentum flux through any enclosing surface | **Corrected / partly verified** [S3]: Lamb (1906) Art. 346, p. 598 states the momentum balance of a **fixed element** (forces plus "flux of matter across the boundary, carrying its momentum with it"). The "any enclosing surface" body-force form was **not found in Lamb**. It is stated in TAN's classical cylinder argument [S9] and used in Wang's proof [S13]. |
598: | Lagally (1922, ZAMM): force on a source/sink = ρ × strength × outside flow | **Verified with conditions** [S10, S13]: *ZAMM* 2(6), 409–422. Lagally's paper is for **steady** flow and states the general dependence (sources, vortices, and the velocity at their location). The explicit `−ρQu₀` form is Wang's restatement, which Wang credits to Lagally "for the special case where the velocity field is steady". Unsteady extensions: [S11, S12]. |
599: | Two steady sinks attract by an inverse square ∝ the product of drain rates | **Verified** [S3, S13]: Lamb Art. 144, p. 192 (like sources attract), and Wang Corollary 4. Lamb's sources are the ends of narrow tubes, so fluid is conserved overall. |
600: | C. A. and V. Bjerknes (1870s–1906, *Fields of Force*): pulsating spheres as a **gravity** analogue | **Corrected** [S16, S17]: *Fields of Force* (1906) draws the analogy to **electric charges and magnetic poles with the sign reversed** (like phases attract), ⛔ not to gravity. The pulsation theory of **gravity** is credited to Kelvin (1871) and C. A. Bjerknes (1871) only by Wikipedia (citing Zenneck 1903), which is secondary only. |
601: | G. I. Taylor (1928): forces on a body in a converging stream | **Verified** [S14]: *Proc. R. Soc. A* 120, 260–283; the "horizontal buoyancy" `−V dp/dx`. Note that the "Taylor theorem" of the Lagally–Taylor–Kirchhoff triad is a different 1928 paper (*Proc. R. Soc. A* 120, 13–21) [S11, S14]. |
602: | Riemann 1853, two fragments, printed 1876 by Dedekind and Weber | **Verified** [S18]: pp. 496–506; edited by H. Weber "unter Mitwirkung von R. Dedekind". "Neue mathematische Principien" carries the footnote "Gefunden am 1. März 1853". |
603: | Riemann: "Gravitation und Licht" tied to his letter of 28 Dec 1853 | **Unverified**: no opened source gives it. |
604: | Riemann: the substance vanishes into "another world" | **Corrected** [S18, S17]: Riemann's word is **"Geisteswelt"** (the mental or spirit world, from Herbart's psychology). "Another world or dimension" is Wikipedia's retelling. |
605: | Riemann: inflow ∝ mass; incompressible, inertia-free; speed ∝ force (so v ∝ 1/r², not the river model's escape speed) | **Verified, from two fragments** [S18]: the drain, "incompressible homogene Flüssigkeit ohne Trägheit" and "seiner Masse proportionale Mengen" are in fragment 3 (dated), which also has a footnote with inflow ∝ the gravitational force; "Geschwindigkeit der Grösse der Kraft proportional" and the inverse-square force he must reproduce (his item 4) are in fragment 2 (undated), whose substance is conserved in each volume element. The river model's escape speed: [S21]. |
606: | Riemann: volume resistance → gravity and electrostatics; line-element resistance → light, heat, magnetism | **Verified** [S18]. The text says "electrodynamische oder magnetische" attraction and repulsion. |
607: | Riemann: stops on how to choose two memory kernels (Bottazzini & Tazzioli) | **Verified from Riemann himself** [S18]: the question near the end (l.38582–38586) is about the two functions weighting a substance element's earlier forms; the fragment then closes on the two-resistance split (l.38607–38616) without choosing them. The Bottazzini & Tazzioli attribution is **not verified** (sample pages only) [S20]. |
608: | Riemann: never computed it, no light-bending number | **Search statement only** [S18]: no deflection term found in pp. 494–506. |
609: | English translation: Baker–Christenson–Orde, *Collected Papers* (2004) | **Not opened.** It appears only in search summaries (Q14), and the MAA review page returned HTTP 521. |
610: | Newton 1675 letter to Oldenburg; 1679 letter to Boyle | 1675 to Oldenburg, "and later to Robert Boyle": **secondary only** [S17]. The year 1679 is **unverified**. |
611: | Soldner (1801): Newtonian deflection, half the GR value | **Corrected** [S23]: written 1801, **published 1804**; GR's prediction is "twice as high". |
612: 
613: ## Checked, not cited
614: 
615: - **R. L. Kirkwood**, "Gravitational Field Equations", *Phys. Rev.* 95, 1051 (1954), DOI 10.1103/PhysRev.95.1051
616:   (APS abstract page, Q17). It gives ether equations of motion from Newton's law; the abstract shows no sink. The
617:   1953 paper named in Q17 was not found.
618: - **I. Simaciu, G. Dumitrescu, Z. Borsos**, "Acoustic force of the gravitational type", arXiv:1905.03622 (2019),
619:   Q23. Abstract: "under certain restrictive conditions, Bjerknes secondary forces are attractive"; "proportionate to
620:   the product of the virtual masses of the two bubbles." Not used (bubble acoustics, no drain).
621: - **Wikipedia, *Bjerknes force*** (Q4): superseded by the primary text [S16].
622: - **St Andrews, C. A. Bjerknes biography** (Q4): the WebFetch summary reports no mention of gravitation. Not used.
623: - **Papadopoulos**, "Physics in Riemann's mathematical papers", arXiv:1711.01755: cites "Gravitation und Licht" at
624:   "p. 532–538" of another edition. Not used; the pages here are from the 1876 edition [S18].
625: - **Analogue-gravity results** for Q19 and Q24 (acoustic black holes, the draining bathtub, analogue lensing): none
626:   treats the motion of the sink or vortex as a body. This is recorded in the section's NOT FOUND list.

64:   35687, and its footnote "Gefunden am 1. März 1853" is at 35706 (P8).

````text
$ python3 research/pde_ledger_v3/scripts/S16_record_measurements.py --lookup M06
FILE research/pde_ledger_v3/scripts/S16_moving_region.py lines 1:EOF
1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """S16 independent SymPy construction: balance IBP and normal-speed transport.
3: 
4: No data or expressions are read from the Wolfram engine. The geometry is a
5: spherical integration chart, with completely general Cartesian live fields.
6: Product-rule integration by parts reduces the supplied PDEs to boundary
7: operators. Named integral/rate functions form an explicitly printed expression
8: graph, including their derivatives; they are never numerical substitutions.
9: """
10: from pathlib import Path
11: from itertools import product
12: import sympy as s
13: 
14: OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'out' / 'S16_moving_region.out'
15: OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
16: log = OUT.open('w')
17: objects = {}
18: 
19: def write(name, value):
20:     log.write(f'{name} = {s.sstr(value)}\n')
21:     log.flush()
22: 
23: def emit(name, value):
24:     write(name, value)
25:     objects[name] = value
26:     write(name + '.comparison', 'nothing to compare it with; no second route')
27: 
28: def working(name):
29:     print('WORKING_ON = ' + name, flush=True)
30:     write('WORKING_ON', name)
31: 
32: # Supplied balances, live fields and allowed control-surface geometry.
33: x = s.symbols('x1:4', real=True)
34: t = s.Symbol('t', real=True)
35: rho = s.Symbol('rho', positive=True)
36: theta, phi = s.symbols('theta phi', real=True)
37: args = (*x, t)
38: c = s.Matrix([s.Function(f'Xc{i}')(t) for i in range(1, 4)])
39: a, b = (s.Function(n)(t) for n in ('r_in', 'R'))
40: Sigma = s.Function('Sigma')(*args)
41: F = s.Matrix([s.Function(f'F{i}')(*args) for i in range(1, 4)])
42: G = s.Matrix([s.Function(f'G{i}')(*args) for i in range(1, 4)])
43: Pi = s.Matrix(3, 3, lambda i, j: s.Function(f'Pi{i+1}{j+1}')(*args))
44: f = s.Matrix([s.Function(f'f{i}')(*args) for i in range(1, 4)])
45: n1, n3, am, ap = [s.Function(n)(*args) for n in ('n1', 'n3', 'a_minus', 'a_plus')]
46: face_balance = (-n1*am, n3*ap)
47: def divergence(vector):
48:     return sum(s.diff(vector[j], x[j]) for j in range(3))
49: material = s.diff(Sigma, t) + divergence(F) + sum(face_balance)
50: momentum = [s.diff(G[i], t) + divergence(Pi.row(i)) - f[i] for i in range(3)]
51: e = s.Matrix([s.sin(theta)*s.cos(phi), s.sin(theta)*s.sin(phi), s.cos(theta)])
52: chart = c + rho*e
53: radii = (a, b)
54: surfaces = [chart.subs(rho, radius) for radius in radii]
55: # Generic requested definitions are applied to the input coordinate objects.
56: y = s.Matrix(x) - c
57: weights = [s.S.One, *y, *(y[i]*y[j] for i, j in product(range(3), repeat=2))]
58: 
59: # Derive the moving-endpoint orientation from Leibniz, not a supplied sign.
60: u = s.Function('radialIntegrand')(rho, t)
61: leibniz_operand = s.Integral(u, (rho, a, b))
62: leibniz_rate = s.diff(leibniz_operand, t)
63: endpoint_coefficients = [s.expand(leibniz_rate).coeff(s.diff(r, t)).coeff(u.subs(rho, r)) for r in radii]
64: jac = s.simplify(chart.jacobian((rho, theta, phi)).det())
65: area_vector = s.simplify(chart.diff(theta).cross(chart.diff(phi)))
66: # Area magnitude on 0<theta<pi; orientation is fixed by the radial chart.
67: area = s.trigsimp(area_vector.dot(chart.diff(rho)))
68: normal = [s.simplify(sign*area_vector/area) for sign in endpoint_coefficients]
69: velocity_c = chart.diff(t)
70: velocity_surfaces = [surface.diff(t) for surface in surfaces]
71: velocity_r = [s.simplify(velocity_surfaces[k] - velocity_c) for k in range(2)]
72: speed_c = [s.simplify(normal[k].dot(velocity_c)) for k in range(2)]
73: speed_r = [s.simplify(normal[k].dot(velocity_r[k])) for k in range(2)]
74: areas = [area.subs(rho, r) for r in radii]
75: 
76: class Volume(s.Function):
77:     nargs = 1
78: 
79: class Surface(s.Function):
80:     nargs = 2
81: 
82: # Surface arguments are chart-pulled; Volume arguments retain bound x.
83: def at(expr, k):
84:     return expr.subs(dict(zip(x, surfaces[k])), simultaneous=True)
85: 
86: def vol(expr):
87:     return Volume(s.expand(expr))
88: 
89: def surf(k, expr):
90:     return Surface(s.Integer(k), s.expand(expr))
91: 
92: write('schema', {'Volume': 'shell integral in x',
93:                  'Surface': 'angular integral of chart-pulled integrand times area',
94:                  'X': 'dipole/N, displacement relative to Xc',
95:                  'shapeChoice': 'concentric spheres; no field symmetry',
96:                  'momentOrderChoice': 2,
97:                  'premises': 'supplied and unfalsifiable',

130: # Geometric differentiation coordinates are independent only while taking
131: # partial derivatives. Restoring them through Subs preserves every live jet,

133: def geometry_partial_rates(expr):

135:     radius_heads = {z.func for z in radii}
136:     jets = sorted((jet for jet in expr.atoms(s.Derivative)
137:                    if jet.expr.func in center_heads | radius_heads
138:                    and all(v == t for v in jet.variables)), key=s.default_sort_key)

142:     slots = tuple(s.Dummy(f'geometry{j}') for j in range(len(geometry)))

144:     # partial time derivative as a total derivative of its restored chart.
145:     field_time = s.Dummy('field_time')
146:     frozen = expr.xreplace(dict(zip(geometry, slots))).xreplace({t: field_time})
147:     def restore(value):
148:         return s.Subs(value, (*slots, field_time), (*geometry, t))
149:     result = {'localEvolution': restore(s.diff(frozen, field_time))}
150:     offset = 0
151:     for label, group in (('centerMotion', center), ('radiusMotion', radial)):
152:         result[label] = s.Add(*(restore(s.diff(frozen, slots[offset+j]))*s.diff(jet, t)
153:                                for j, jet in enumerate(group)))
154:         offset += len(group)
155:     return result

157: # Generic product-rule integration by parts, component by component. The
158: # coefficient of each flux derivative is extracted from the solved PDE.
159: def build_rate(name, weight, density, flux, balance, sources):
160:     working(name)
161:     local = s.solve(balance, s.diff(density, t))[0]
162:     raw = s.expand(s.diff(weight*density, t).subs(s.diff(density, t), local))
163:     bulk = raw
164:     currents = []
165:     for j in range(3):
166:         jet = s.diff(flux[j], x[j])
167:         coefficient = bulk.coeff(jet)
168:         currents.append(coefficient*flux[j])
169:         bulk = s.expand(bulk - coefficient*jet - s.diff(coefficient, x[j])*flux[j])
170:     write(name+'.localRate', local)
171:     write(name+'.weightedLocalRate', raw)
172:     write(name+'.afterParts.bulk', bulk)
173:     write(name+'.afterParts.current', currents)
174:     parts = {}
175:     remainder = bulk
176:     for source_name, source in sources:
177:         selected = sum(term for term in s.Add.make_args(bulk) if term.has(source))
178:         parts['bulk.'+source_name] = vol(selected)
179:         remainder = s.expand(remainder-selected)
180:     reference_rates = geometry_partial_rates(weight)
181:     for origin in ('centerMotion', 'radiusMotion'):
182:         reference = s.expand(density*reference_rates[origin].doit())
183:         parts['bulk.reference.'+origin] = vol(reference)
184:         remainder = s.expand(remainder-reference)
185:     parts['bulk.weight'] = vol(remainder)
186:     for k in range(2):
187:         parts[f'surface{k}.rest'] = surf(k, at(s.Matrix(currents).dot(normal[k]), k))
188:         parts[f'surface{k}.centerMotion'] = surf(k, at(weight*density, k)*speed_c[k])
189:         parts[f'surface{k}.radiusMotion'] = surf(k, at(weight*density, k)*speed_r[k])
190:     for part, value in parts.items():
191:         emit(name+'.'+part, value)
192:     emit(name+'.rate', s.Add(*parts.values()))
193:     emit(name+'.integratedForceCompanion', [vol(v) for v in f])
194:     return parts

218: # Time differentiation uses normal-speed volume transport and differentiation
219: # of each surface pullback and area measure. All surface pullbacks are live,
220: # so differentiation also retains spatial jets and the changing area.
221: def integral_time(expr):
222:     if isinstance(expr, Volume):
223:         density = expr.args[0]
224:         return vol(s.diff(density, t)) + s.Add(*(surf(k, at(density, k)*speed)
225:                     for k in range(2) for speed in (speed_c[k], speed_r[k])))
226:     if isinstance(expr, Surface):
227:         k, density = expr.args
228:         k = int(k)
229:         return surf(k, s.diff(density*areas[k], t)/areas[k])
230:     if expr.is_Add:
231:         return s.Add(*(integral_time(term) for term in expr.args))
232:     if expr.is_Mul:
233:         factors = expr.args
234:         return s.Add(*(integral_time(factor)*s.Mul(*(factors[:i]+factors[i+1:]))
235:                        for i, factor in enumerate(factors)))
236:     if expr.is_Pow:
237:         return s.diff(expr, expr.base)*integral_time(expr.base)
238:     return s.diff(expr, t)

240: # The local derivative holds all geometric positions and jets fixed. Volume
241: # transport is then applied to the full integrand as a coefficient; products
242: # of existing velocities with boundary speed stay with the moving boundary.
243: def integral_time_parts(expr):
244:     if isinstance(expr, Volume):
245:         density = expr.args[0]
246:         rates = geometry_partial_rates(density)
247:         pieces = {'localEvolution': vol(rates['localEvolution']),
248:                   'bulk.centerMotion': vol(rates['centerMotion']),
249:                   'bulk.radiusMotion': vol(rates['radiusMotion'])}
250:         for k in range(2):
251:             pieces[f'surface{k}.centerMotion'] = surf(k, at(density, k)*speed_c[k])
252:             pieces[f'surface{k}.radiusMotion'] = surf(k, at(density, k)*speed_r[k])
253:         return pieces
254:     if isinstance(expr, Surface):
255:         k, density = expr.args
256:         k = int(k)
257:         rates = geometry_partial_rates(density*areas[k])
258:         return {('localEvolution' if origin == 'localEvolution' else f'surface{k}.'+origin):
259:                 surf(k, value/areas[k]) for origin, value in rates.items()}
260:     raise TypeError(f'unsupported integral operator {expr.func}')

262: # A comparison within this engine: direct differentiation versus the sum of
263: # origin parts. Linearity groups residuals under their original measures.
264: # Canonicalizing evaluated Subs after differentiation reconciles dummy
265: # differentiation coordinates without prescribing a value for the residual.
266: def integral_residual(left, right):
267:     delta = s.expand(left-right)
268:     integrals = sorted(delta.atoms(Volume, Surface), key=s.default_sort_key)
269:     result = {'outsideIntegrals': delta,
270:               'volumeIntegrand': s.S.Zero,
271:               **{f'surface{k}Integrand': s.S.Zero for k in range(2)}}
272:     for integral in integrals:
273:         coefficient = delta.coeff(integral)
274:         result['outsideIntegrals'] -= coefficient*integral
275:         if isinstance(integral, Volume):
276:             result['volumeIntegrand'] += coefficient*integral.args[0]
277:         else:
278:             result[f'surface{int(integral.args[0])}Integrand'] += coefficient*integral.args[1]
279:     return {key: s.simplify(value.doit()) for key, value in result.items()}

359: def units(expr, env=None):
360:     env = coordinate_units if env is None else env
361:     if expr == 0:
362:         return frozenset()  # an additive zero has no unique physical dimension
363:     if expr.is_Number or expr == s.pi:
364:         return frozenset([s.S.One])
365:     if expr in env:
366:         return frozenset([env[expr]])
367:     if isinstance(expr, Volume):
368:         return frozenset(s.cancel(u*L**3) for u in units(expr.args[0], env))
369:     if isinstance(expr, Surface):
370:         return frozenset(s.cancel(u*L**2) for u in units(expr.args[1], env))
371:     if isinstance(expr, s.Subs):
372:         mapping = dict(env)
373:         for var, point in zip(expr.variables, expr.point):
374:             mapping[var] = next(iter(units(point, env)))
375:         return units(expr.expr, mapping)
376:     if isinstance(expr, s.Derivative):
377:         dims = units(expr.expr, env)
378:         for var, order in expr.variable_count:
379:             dims = frozenset(s.cancel(dim/env[var]**order) for dim in dims)
380:         return dims
381:     if expr.is_Add:
382:         return frozenset().union(*(units(term, env) for term in expr.args))
383:     if expr.is_Mul:
384:         choices = [units(term, env) for term in expr.args]
385:         return frozenset(s.cancel(s.prod(parts)) for parts in product(*choices))
386:     if expr.is_Pow:
387:         return frozenset(s.cancel(unit**expr.exp) for unit in units(expr.base, env))
388:     if expr.func in (s.sin, s.cos):
389:         return frozenset([s.S.One])
390:     if expr.func in field_units:
391:         return frozenset([field_units[expr.func]])
392:     raise TypeError(f'unregistered dimensional node: {s.sstr(expr)}')

394: def leaves(value):
395:     if isinstance(value, dict):
396:         for key, part in value.items():
397:             for path, item in leaves(part):
398:                 yield (str(key), *path), item
399:     elif isinstance(value, (list, tuple, s.MatrixBase)):
400:         for i, part in enumerate(value):
401:             for path, item in leaves(part):
402:                 yield (str(i), *path), item
403:     elif isinstance(value, s.Equality):
404:         yield ('lhs',), value.lhs
405:         yield ('rhs',), value.rhs
406:     else:
407:         yield (), value

409: def dimensional_sums(expr, env=None):
410:     env = coordinate_units if env is None else env
411:     if isinstance(expr, s.Subs):
412:         context = dict(env)
413:         for var, point in zip(expr.variables, expr.point):
414:             context[var] = next(iter(units(point, env)))
415:         yield from dimensional_sums(expr.expr, context)
416:         for point in expr.point:
417:             yield from dimensional_sums(point, env)
418:         return
419:     if expr.is_Add:
420:         yield expr, env
421:     for child in expr.args:
422:         if isinstance(child, s.Basic):
423:             yield from dimensional_sums(child, env)

60: (* Partial differentiation in independent geometric jet coordinates. Every
61:    geometric jet present in the operand is included, with no degree bound.
62:    Restoring the jets retains their live time dependence. These coordinates
63:    distinguish field evolution from derivatives of the moving reference. *)
64: geometryHeads = Join[{c1, c2, c3}, {rin, rout}];
65: geometryChain[z_] := Module[{jets, center, radial, geometry, slots, frozen, restore, rate},
66:  jets = DeleteDuplicates[Cases[z, Derivative[n_][h_][t] /; MemberQ[geometryHeads, h], {0, Infinity}]];
67:  center = Join[cc, Select[jets, MemberQ[{c1, c2, c3}, #[[0, 1]]] &]];
68:  radial = Join[radii, Select[jets, MemberQ[{rin, rout}, #[[0, 1]]] &]];
69:  geometry = Join[center, radial]; slots = Table[Unique["geometry"], Length[geometry]];
70:  frozen = z /. Thread[geometry -> slots];
71:  restore[v_] := v /. Thread[slots -> geometry];
72:  rate[group_] := Total[Map[Function[g, restore[D[frozen, slots[[First[FirstPosition[geometry, g]]]]]] D[g, t]], group]];
73:  <|"localEvolution" -> restore[D[frozen, t]], "centerMotion" -> rate[center], "radiusMotion" -> rate[radial]|>];
74: windowRates = geometryChain[window];
75: 
76: (* Weak differentiation has separate operands for the weighted local law
77:    and the moving window. Only the former undergoes spatial integration by
78:    parts. Window motion is differentiated before multiplying the integrand;
79:    its origin therefore does not depend on the integrand's velocity degree. *)
80: windowRules = Join[Thread[(HeavisideTheta /@ level) -> {h1, h2}], Thread[(DiracDelta /@ level) -> {d1, d2}]];
81: windowPolynomial[z_] := Expand[z /. windowRules];
82: reduceWindow[z_] := Module[{p = windowPolynomial[z]},
83:  {Coefficient[Coefficient[p, h1], h2] /. {d1 -> 0, d2 -> 0},
84:   Table[at[k, Coefficient[p, {d1, d2}[[k]]] /. {h1 -> 1, h2 -> 1, d1 -> 0, d2 -> 0}], {k, 2}]}];
85: weak[w_, den_, flux_, balance_] := Module[{localRate, raw, integrated, jet, coeff, rest, reduced},
86:  localRate = First[Solve[balance == 0, D[den, t]]];
87:  raw = Expand[D[w den window, t] /. localRate];
88:  integrated = Expand[window (D[w den, t] /. localRate)];
89:  Do[jet = D[flux[[j]], xx[[j]]]; coeff = Coefficient[integrated, jet];
90:     integrated = Expand[integrated - coeff jet - D[coeff, xx[[j]]] flux[[j]]], {j, 3}];
91:  rest = reduceWindow[integrated]; reduced = reduceWindow[integrated + w den D[window, t]];
92:  <|"localRate" -> localRate, "windowDerivative" -> raw, "afterParts" -> Expand[integrated + w den D[window, t]],
93:    "reduced" -> reduced, "rest" -> rest,
94:    "centerMotion" -> reduceWindow[w den windowRates["centerMotion"]],
95:    "radiusMotion" -> reduceWindow[w den windowRates["radiusMotion"]]|>];
96: 
97: terms[z_] := If[Head[Expand[z]] === Plus, List @@ Expand[z], {Expand[z]}];
98: selectTerms[z_, heads_] := Total[Select[terms[z], !FreeQ[#, Alternatives @@ heads] &]];
99: rateParts[tag_, w_, den_, flux_, balance_, sources_] := Module[{derivation, body, components, picked, remainder, reference},
100:  working[tag]; derivation = weak[w, den, flux, balance];
101:  write[tag <> ".derivation", KeyDrop[derivation, {"reduced", "rest", "centerMotion", "radiusMotion"}]];
102:  body = derivation["reduced"][[1]]; remainder = body; components = <||>;
103:  Do[picked = selectTerms[body, {sources[[k]]}]; remainder = Expand[remainder - picked];
104:     AssociateTo[components, "bulkSource" <> ToString[k] -> V[picked]], {k, Length[sources]}];
105:  reference = geometryChain[w];
106:  Do[picked = Expand[den reference[origin]]; remainder = Expand[remainder - picked];
107:     AssociateTo[components, "bulkReference." <> origin -> V[picked]], {origin, {"centerMotion", "radiusMotion"}}];
108:  AssociateTo[components, "bulkWeight" -> V[remainder]];
109:  Do[Do[AssociateTo[components, "surface" <> ToString[k] <> "." <> origin -> B[k, derivation[origin][[2, k]]]],
110:        {origin, {"rest", "centerMotion", "radiusMotion"}}], {k, 2}];
111:  KeyValueMap[emit[tag <> "." <> #1, #2] &, components];
112:  emit[tag <> ".rate", Total[Values[components]]];
113:  emit[tag <> ".integratedForceCompanion", V /@ force]; components];
114: 
115: working["moments"];
116: weights = Join[{1}, yy, Flatten[Outer[Times, yy, yy]]];
117: moments = (V[Expand[# density]] &) /@ weights;
118: Do[emit["moment." <> ToString[k - 1], moments[[k]]], {k, Length[moments]}];
119: write["moment.indices", Join[{{}}, List /@ Range[3], Tuples[Range[3], 2]]];
120: emit["count.definition", count[t] -> First[moments]];
121: Do[emit["dipole.definition." <> ToString[i], dip[i][t] -> moments[[i + 1]]], {i, 3}];
122: Do[emit["momentum.definition." <> ToString[i], mom[i][t] -> V[momentumDensity[[i]]]], {i, 3}];
123: countParts = rateParts["count", 1, density, materialFlux, materialBalance, {n1, n3}];
124: dipParts = Table[rateParts["dipole." <> ToString[i], yy[[i]], density, materialFlux, materialBalance, {n1, n3}], {i, 3}];
125: pParts = Table[rateParts["momentum." <> ToString[i], 1, momentumDensity[[i]], momentumFlux[[i]], momentumBalance[[i]], {Head[force[[i]]]}], {i, 3}];
126: working["momentumReceived"];
127: received = Table[Total[Lookup[pParts[[i]], {"bulkSource1", "surface1.rest", "surface2.rest"}]], {i, 3}];
128: emit["momentumReceived", received];
129: emit["momentumRate", Total[Values[#]] & /@ pParts];
130: emit["momentumSurfaceMotion", KeyTake[#, {"surface1.centerMotion", "surface1.radiusMotion", "surface2.centerMotion", "surface2.radiusMotion"}] & /@ pParts];
131: 
132: (* Differentiate the unevaluated integrals by their measures. Volume
133:    transport is derived again from the window derivative with no PDE. *)
134: volTime[z_] := Module[{red = reduceWindow[D[z window, t]]}, V[red[[1]]] + Sum[B[k, red[[2, k]]], {k, 2}]];
135: boundTime[k_, z_] := B[k, Expand[D[z area[[k]], t]/area[[k]]]];
136: time[z_Plus] := Total[time /@ (List @@ z)];
137: time[z_Times] := Module[{f = List @@ z}, Total[MapIndexed[time[#1] Times @@ Delete[f, First[#2]] &, f]]];
138: time[z_Power] := z[[2]] z[[1]]^(z[[2]] - 1) time[z[[1]]];
139: time[V[z_]] := volTime[z];
140: time[B[k_, z_]] := boundTime[k, z];
141: time[z_] := D[z, t];
142: (* Substitute the governed Sigma time jet at arbitrary live arguments;
143:    rates of F, n, a and f have no supplied evolution and remain derivatives. *)
144: (* The integrand and the integration domain are differentiated separately.
145:    A motion jet in z is a coefficient of the window derivative, not another
146:    attribution for it. This preserves squares and mixed velocity products. *)
147: timeParts[V[z_]] := Module[{local = geometryChain[z], result, red},
148:  result = <|"localEvolution" -> V[local["localEvolution"]],
149:             "bulk.centerMotion" -> V[local["centerMotion"]],
150:             "bulk.radiusMotion" -> V[local["radiusMotion"]]|>;
151:  Do[red = reduceWindow[z windowRates[origin]];
152:     Do[AssociateTo[result, "surface" <> ToString[k] <> "." <> origin -> B[k, red[[2, k]]]], {k, 2}],
153:     {origin, {"centerMotion", "radiusMotion"}}]; result];
154: timeParts[B[k_, z_]] := Module[{local = geometryChain[z area[[k]]]},
155:  <|"localEvolution" -> B[k, Expand[local["localEvolution"]/area[[k]]]],
156:    "surface" <> ToString[k] <> ".centerMotion" -> B[k, Expand[local["centerMotion"]/area[[k]]]],
157:    "surface" <> ToString[k] <> ".radiusMotion" -> B[k, Expand[local["radiusMotion"]/area[[k]]]]|>];
158: (* Linear integral comparison: residuals are integrands on the same printed
159:    measures. The operands are the direct product derivative and the sum of
160:    the separately differentiated origins. No expected-value guard is used. *)
161: integralResidual[left_, right_] := Module[{delta = Expand[left - right], vs, bs, all, residual},
162:  vs = DeleteDuplicates[Cases[delta, _V, {0, Infinity}]];
163:  bs = Table[DeleteDuplicates[Cases[delta, B[k, _], {0, Infinity}]], {k, 2}];
164:  all = Join[vs, Flatten[bs]];
165:  residual = <|"outsideIntegrals" -> Expand[delta - Total[(Coefficient[delta, #] # &) /@ all]],
166:                "volumeIntegrand" -> Cancel[Total[(Coefficient[delta, #] #[[1]] &) /@ vs]]|>;
167:  Do[AssociateTo[residual, "surface" <> ToString[k] <> "Integrand" -> Cancel[Total[(Coefficient[delta, #] #[[2]] &) /@ bs[[k]]]]], {k, 2}]; residual];
168: partitionReport[tag_, direct_, pieces_Association] := Module[{total = Total[Values[pieces]], residual},
169:  write[tag <> ".direct", direct]; AssociateTo[objects, tag <> ".direct" -> direct];
170:  write[tag <> ".partsSum", total]; AssociateTo[objects, tag <> ".partsSum" -> total];
171:  residual = integralResidual[direct, total];
172:  write[tag <> ".residual", residual];
173:  write[tag <> ".routes", {"direct product derivative", "chain-rule origins and window-only motion"}]];
174: materialRHS = D[density, t] /. First[Solve[materialBalance == 0, D[density, t]]];
175: governed[z_] := z /. Derivative[0, 0, 0, 1][Sigma][u_, v_, w_, s_] :> (materialRHS /. Thread[args -> {u, v, w, s}]);
176: working["centerKinematics"];
177: rateAliases = <||>; derivativeAliases = <||>;
178: bindParts[p_, prefix_] := Association[KeyValueMap[Function[{key, value}, Module[{name = Symbol[prefix <> StringReplace[key, "." -> ""]][t], dv, pieces},
179:  emit[prefix <> ".term." <> key, name -> value]; dv = governed[time[value]];
180:  emit[prefix <> ".termRate." <> key, D[name, t] -> dv];
181:  pieces = Map[governed, timeParts[value]];
182:  KeyValueMap[emit[prefix <> ".termRatePart." <> key <> "." <> #1, #2] &, pieces];
183:  partitionReport[prefix <> ".termRatePartition." <> key, dv, pieces];
184:  AssociateTo[rateAliases, name -> value]; AssociateTo[derivativeAliases, D[name, t] -> dv]; key -> name]], p]];
185: namesN = bindParts[countParts, "nrate"];
186: namesD = Table[bindParts[dipParts[[i]], "drate" <> ToString[i]], {i, 3}];
187: replacementRates = Join[{Derivative[1][count][t] -> Total[Values[namesN]]}, Table[Derivative[1][dip[i]][t] -> Total[Values[namesD[[i]]]], {i, 3}]];
188: replacementSeconds = Join[{Derivative[2][count][t] -> Total[D[Values[namesN], t]]}, Table[Derivative[2][dip[i]][t] -> Total[D[Values[namesD[[i]]], t]], {i, 3}]];
189: relativeCenter = Table[Divide[dip[i][t], count[t]], {i, 3}];
190: absoluteCenter = MapThread[Plus, {cc, relativeCenter}];
191: emit["center.relative.definition", relativeCenter];
192: emit["center.absolute.definition", absoluteCenter];
193: emit["center.relative.rate", Expand[D[relativeCenter, t] /. replacementRates]];
194: emit["center.relative.acceleration", Expand[D[relativeCenter, {t, 2}] /. replacementSeconds /. replacementRates]];
195: emit["center.absolute.rate", Expand[D[absoluteCenter, t] /. replacementRates]];
196: emit["center.absolute.acceleration", Expand[D[absoluteCenter, {t, 2}] /. replacementSeconds /. replacementRates]];
197: emit["count.rateForNormalization", Total[Values[namesN]]];
198: emit["count.accelerationForNormalization", Total[D[Values[namesN], t]]];
199: 
200: (* Dimension vectors use independent length, time, count, momentum units.
201:    Momentum is an independent unit: no mass or count-to-momentum law.
202:    Field dimensions are solved from the supplied balance terms; face-factor
203:    dimensions are velocity dimensions. No numerical value is tested. *)
204: working["dimensions"];
205: baseDim = <|x1 -> {1, 0, 0, 0}, x2 -> {1, 0, 0, 0}, x3 -> {1, 0, 0, 0}, t -> {0, 1, 0, 0}, rho -> {1, 0, 0, 0}, theta -> {0, 0, 0, 0}, phi -> {0, 0, 0, 0}|>;
206: fieldDim = <||>;
207: Do[AssociateTo[fieldDim, h -> {1, 0, 0, 0}], {h, {c1, c2, c3, rin, rout}}];
208: AssociateTo[fieldDim, Sigma -> {-3, 0, 1, 0}];
209: Do[AssociateTo[fieldDim, h -> {-3, 0, 0, 1}], {h, {G1, G2, G3}}];
210: Do[AssociateTo[fieldDim, h -> {1, -1, 0, 0}], {h, {aminus, aplus}}];
211: Do[AssociateTo[fieldDim, h -> (fieldDim[Sigma] - baseDim[t] + baseDim[x1])], {h, {F1, F2, F3}}];
212: Do[AssociateTo[fieldDim, h -> (fieldDim[G1] - baseDim[t] + baseDim[x1])], {h, Flatten[piHeads]}];
213: Do[AssociateTo[fieldDim, h -> (fieldDim[G1] - baseDim[t])], {h, {f1, f2, f3}}];
214: Do[AssociateTo[fieldDim, h -> (fieldDim[Sigma] - baseDim[t] - fieldDim[aminus])], {h, {n1, n3}}];
215: AssociateTo[fieldDim, count -> (fieldDim[Sigma] + 3 baseDim[x1])];
216: Do[AssociateTo[fieldDim, dip[i] -> (fieldDim[count] + baseDim[x1])]; AssociateTo[fieldDim, mom[i] -> (fieldDim[G1] + 3 baseDim[x1])], {i, 3}];
217: write["dimensions.basis", {"length", "time", "count", "momentum"}]; write["dimensions.fields", fieldDim];
218: dimension[0] := {};
219: dimension[z_?NumberQ] := {{0, 0, 0, 0}};
220: dimension[Pi] := {{0, 0, 0, 0}};
221: dimension[z_Symbol] := {Lookup[baseDim, z, Missing["dimension", z]]};
222: dimension[z_Plus] := DeleteDuplicates[Join @@ (dimension /@ (List @@ z))];
223: dimension[z_Times] := Fold[DeleteDuplicates[Flatten[Outer[Plus, #1, #2, 1], 1]] &, {{0, 0, 0, 0}}, (dimension /@ (List @@ z))];
224: dimension[z_Power] := (# z[[2]] &) /@ dimension[z[[1]]];
225: dimension[Sin[_] | Cos[_] | HeavisideTheta[_]] := {{0, 0, 0, 0}};
226: dimension[V[z_]] := (# + 3 baseDim[x1] &) /@ dimension[z];
227: dimension[B[_, z_]] := (# + 2 baseDim[x1] &) /@ dimension[z];
228: dimension[Derivative[orders__][h_][ar___]] := Module[{dd = Lookup[fieldDim, h, Missing["dimension", h]], av = {ar}},
229:  {dd - Total[MapThread[Times, {{orders}, If[Length[av] == 1, {baseDim[t]}, Append[ConstantArray[baseDim[x1], 3], baseDim[t]]]}]]}];
230: dimension[z_Rule] := {dimension[First[z]], dimension[Last[z]]};
231: dimension[z_List] := dimension /@ z;
232: dimension[z_Association] := Map[dimension, z];
233: dimension[z_] := {Lookup[fieldDim, Head[z], Missing["dimension", HoldForm[z]]]};
234: KeyValueMap[(AssociateTo[fieldDim, Head[#1] -> (If[StringStartsQ[SymbolName[Head[#1]], "nrate"], fieldDim[count], fieldDim[dip[1]]] - baseDim[t])]) &, rateAliases];
235: (* For every printed object emit the inferred dimensional operands. For
236:    each sum in its tree also emit dimensional differences, unconditionally;
237:    these are dimensional homogeneity data, not expected-value guards. *)
238: KeyValueMap[Function[{tag, value}, Module[{sums, ds},
239:  write[tag <> ".dimensions", dimension[value]];
240:  sums = Cases[value, z_Plus :> z, {0, Infinity}];
241:  Do[ds = dimension /@ (List @@ sums[[k]]);
242:  write[tag <> ".dimensionSum." <> ToString[k] <> ".operands", ds];
243:  write[tag <> ".dimensionSum." <> ToString[k] <> ".residuals", If[MemberQ[ds, {}, Infinity], Missing["zeroTerm"], Map[# - First[ds] &, ds]]], {k, Length[sums]}]]], objects];
244: write["coverage.objects", Keys[objects]];
245: write["coverage.ungovernedRates", {F1, F2, F3, n1, n3, aminus, aplus}];
246: write["coverage.fluxDecomposition", Missing["NoSuppliedLaw", "Pi has no separately supplied stress or advection constituents"]];
247: Close[stream];
248: Print["TRANSCRIPT = ", outfile];
249: Exit[0];
````

## Why this exists

v3 is requirements-first: each sector states what it needs, and the knit happens last. The light sector
(S9, S10, S11, S11b) is built on **S1–S8, none of which have been run** — there are no step records for
them. That is the design, not an oversight: the substrate gets built once every sector has said what it
requires, so it can be checked against all of them at once rather than rebuilt per sector.

The bet only pays if the requirements are **captured**. Measured 2026-08-05: exactly two obligations are
recorded, both from S11, both about one quantity, both as inline anchors in a 1200-line plan. Everything
else a built sector assumes about the substrate is implicit prose spread across four step records.

`DEFECT_REGISTER.md` records what is *wrong*. `ANSATZ_LEDGER.md` records what is *postulated and not
derived*. Neither records **what a later step must deliver for an earlier result to stand.** That is this
file.

## The failure this prevents

At Phase 5 the sectors are knitted and the substrate is built against their combined requirements. If a
requirement was never written down, one of two things happens: the substrate is built without it and the
sector's result silently loses its footing, or it is rediscovered late and the substrate is rebuilt. Both
were survivable with one sector. With five they are not.

The S7 entry below is the shape of the problem. Standing at S7, the honest answer is "the slab width is
not selected" — a real result, bankable, and **insufficient**. Only S11 knows that the question must be
asked again with the width made position- and time-dependent. Nobody at S7 would think to ask.

## Entry schema

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | stable identifier, cited from both ends |
| `source` | the step that needs it |
| `target` | the step that must deliver it |
| `requirement` | **the object required**, named — not a derivation path for it |
| `on failure` | what breaks in the source step if the target cannot deliver |
| `status` | OPEN · DELIVERED · RETIRED (with the commit that changed it) |

Name the object; do not prescribe how the target should obtain it. A requirement that specifies a
derivation route manufactures arguments about the route — see `CLAUDE.md` rule 3.

Distinguish carefully:
- a **requirement** is an obligation on a *future* step;
- a **postulate** is a value or form assumed *here* and not derived — that belongs in `ANSATZ_LEDGER.md`;
- a **defect** is something already wrong — that belongs in `DEFECT_REGISTER.md`.

A postulate with a named retirement condition generates a requirement. `B_comp` below is exactly that.

### R-S1-02 — the substructure's shear response, as a function of the order parameter

### R-S8-01 — the form of the brane's quadratic stiffness functional

  valid representatives; no individual representative coefficient is the required object. Its

  ⭐ Note this is the `(u_L, h)` block — the scalar sector — so it bears on the **longitudinal** slot and

### R-S8-04 — what carries the brane's internal angular momentum

- **source** O2 (`steps/O2_steady_brane_balance.md`, register handoff); S9, S10, S11 · **target** S8 · **status** OPEN
- **requirement** — the object in the substructure that carries **internal angular momentum** on the brane,
  or the couple-stress it supports. ⛔ Not a mechanism, ⛔ not a model: the object, or a statement that there
  is none.
- **on failure** — ⛔⛔ **the curl-only stiffness functional is not an admissible continuum mechanics.** An
  energy in `(∇×u)²` alone has an **antisymmetric** Cauchy stress, and balance of angular momentum forces
  the Cauchy stress to be **symmetric** unless the medium carries distributed couples or internal spin. If
  the substructure supplies neither, the light sector's central form is inadmissible **regardless of its
  mode content** — S9's and S10's mode counts, dimensions and speeds would all be computed from a
  functional no medium can have.
- **note** — ⚠ **This is the objection that sank MacCullagh's aether**, and it is the one part of that
  theory the 19th century never answered: Stokes pressed it, and Kelvin's gyrostatic models were attempts to
  supply exactly this object. ⇒ ⭐ **prior art is the oracle here** — it tells us the obligation is real and
  that answers exist, ⛔ it tells us nothing about whether **ours** delivers one ⇒ `CLAUDE.md` rule 16.
  ⭐ Known families a delivered answer might fall into, ⛔ **none assumed and none prescribed**: continua
  with an independent microrotation degree of freedom (Cosserat/micropolar), and media with stored internal
  angular momentum.
  ⛔ **One family is the wrong one and should not be reached for:** modern *odd elasticity* buys an
  antisymmetric modulus tensor by making the solid **active and non-conservative**. MacCullagh's medium is
  **conservative** — it has a genuine energy functional — so a non-conservative realisation would be
  answering a different question.
  ⚠ `R-S8-01` asks for the **form** and is silent on admissibility; a substructure could deliver the
  curl-only form and still owe this.
- **O2 scope** — OPEN `𝒜_rot^live` carries this existing S8 obligation, including whether internal
  angular momentum/couple stress is present. O2 selects no stress symmetry or carrier and does not
  establish a curl-only live stress. The original conservative-MacCullagh objection keeps its
  original domain; it is not newly proved for an unspecified viscoelastic stress. The O2 addition
  carries the explicitly required carrier/admissibility question within its named material and
  corresponding power accounting; it adds no flowing constitutive response form. The accounting
  remains conditional with that question OPEN
  (`directives/O2_SHARED_PHYSICS.md`, §§3.2, 4, 6).

### R-S8-05 — the frame the brane's rotational stiffness is measured against

- **source** O2 (`steps/O2_steady_brane_balance.md`, register handoff); S9, S10, S11 · **target** S8 · **status** OPEN
- **requirement** — the frame with respect to which the brane's rotational stiffness is defined: **what
  `∇×u` is measured against.**
- **on failure** — for an infinitesimal rigid rotation `u = ω × r` the curl is `2ω ≠ 0`, so a curl-only
  energy is **nonzero when the whole medium is turned**. ⇒ if the reference is external, the medium knows
  an absolute orientation, and every result in the sector inherits a preferred-orientation signature that
  something later must hide. ⛔ That is a falsifiable consequence, ⛔ not a philosophical discomfort.
- **note** — ⭐ **A brane may escape this where a bulk aether cannot**, and the difference is the whole
  point of the entry. For a bulk medium *"rotation relative to what"* has no local answer — the 1839
  objection. For a **domain wall**, the wall supplies its own local frame (its normal, its induced
  geometry), rotation relative to the wall is meaningful and local, and rotating everything rotates the wall
  too ⇒ the stiffness would be **relative**, and the objection would not arise.
  ⚠⚠ **That is a HYPOTHESIS, ⛔ not a result.** Nothing in the corpus computes it. The slab-in-bulk
  calculation is where it is settled ⇒ **S11b-A** (interface response) is the existing partial artifact,
  built under the old pattern and on the rebuild list.
  ⚠ **A flowing medium does NOT answer this.** Flow bears on the **velocity** frame — whether a background
  drift is detectable — and the analog-gravity route hides it in an effective metric. ⛔ Orientation is a
  **separate** objection: being carried is not being turned. ⇒ ⭐ do not let one argument discharge both.
- **O2 scope** — OPEN `𝒜_rot^live` retains the physical rotational frame as an existing S8
  obligation explicitly carried by the spec. Neither radial flow, the graph normal nor LAB_HELD
  chooses that material frame. O2's named force/power accounting retains the frame question OPEN;
  this addition supplies no frame or new rotational-response form. O2 does not extend the original
  curl-only objection to an unspecified live stress
  (`directives/O2_SHARED_PHYSICS.md`, §§1, 3.2, 6, 7).

### R-S22-01 — how the energy a throat releases splits among light, the extra wave and the bulk

- **source**
  - S11 (`steps/S11_stray_longitudinal.md`, departure table and the paragraphs after it). The table gives the
    question "whether matter directly observes the second cone" the owner "derived matter/interface
    coupling". The record says "A second cone is only a departure if matter COUPLES to it", and describes
    matter as "a throat held open by a trapped brane-shear standing wave".
  - The photon survey, E32–E34 and E38 (`PHOTON_POLARIZATION_SURVEY.md` §4). Each is "In apparent conflict",
    under conditions that differ by entry. In the survey's words, the classification rests on "E32–E34 on
    matter coupling and, for the blackbody comparison, ordinary thermal-radiation participation; E38
    additionally on the extra branch's cosmological relativistic population, energy/perturbation mapping and
    decoupling history". (C6, C7.)
- **target** S22 (the nonlinear throat solve), together with Q2 (the mouth source and its held datum) and
  S12 (the throat's order-conversion source and its boundary data). These owners were chosen by the user on
  2026-10-19; the S11 record itself names only "derived matter/interface coupling". (C8.)
  The user's 2026-10-20 **"Keep S12"** decision retains every owner. S12 stays OPEN for its
  forms, delivered only after the brane is defined following the force sectors; this requirements
  record delivers none of those forms (S12 record §§5–7, retrieval M18).
- **status** OPEN
- **requirement** — Consider a throat held open by its trapped shear wave. The trapped-wave state can change,
  the throat can move, and its mouth can change shape. When any of these happens, the object is the energy
  released, with its frequency content and rate, and how it splits among three channels:
  - the free transverse waves (light);
  - the extra longitudinal wave (S11's second cone);
  - the bulk.

  The entry also requires the reverse: how much of the energy each channel carries in is taken up by a
  throat, at each frequency.
- **on failure** — S11's departure cannot be classified. The record makes the second cone a departure only
  if matter couples to it, and without these objects nothing decides whether matter observes it. E32–E34
  and E38 stay "in apparent conflict", with their condition undecided.
- **note: what a delivered split would and would not decide** —
  - **Each measurement has its own conditions** (survey §4):
    - **E33**, the laboratory blackbody, needs the extra wave to be an additional ordinary thermal mode,
      with the usual occupation, energy and dispersion, and a calibrated emission and absorption response.
    - **E34**, the CMB spectrum, needs its power to enter the calibrated CMB radiance rather than cancel in
      the sky/reference comparison.
    - **E38**, `N_eff`, needs it to be extra gravitating radiation, populated and relativistic in the early
      universe. The survey adds that a weak population or earlier decoupling is not generically excluded.
  - **The split alone decides none of them.** Whether the extra wave is populated depends on several things:
    - its emission and uptake rates, compared with each measurement's timescale;
    - its escape into the bulk;
    - its initial population and the expansion history.

    What a populated wave then carries depends on its own speed. In S11 that speed is set by `B_comp/ρ_br`
    (`R-S6-01`), not by light's `μ_R/ρ_br`. So a share comparable to light's is not by itself a conflict,
    and neither is equilibrium with matter. Nor does a small share by itself rule one out.
  - **The falsifier** is each measurement, applied under its own conditions to the population and power
    that these objects, the extra wave's speed and its escape into the bulk predict. That application is
    later work. This entry states no bound; compare the note in `R-S12-01`.
  - **The quantum part.** The survey's conditions also assume the usual quantum occupation. The plan
    assigns that to a separate project (`V3_STEP_PLAN.md:1198–1204`; survey [P8]), so a classical split
    does not settle that part. (C7.)
- **relation** —
  - S22's linear test 1 asks how much light passing a supplied defect profile converts into the
    longitudinal mode. S11c asked how much light converts where the brane changes (`V3_STEP_PLAN.md:508`).
    Both concern incoming light; neither is a throat's own emission.
  - S22's linear test 2 asks whether the longitudinal mode radiates into the bulk, and needs the interface
    law (`V3_STEP_PLAN.md:1181`). That escape enters the extra wave's population. So applying any
    measurement under this entry also needs test 2's result.
  - The S11 record adds that at homogeneous linear order "the mode's bulk leakage and direct observability
    require the brane–bulk interface law". S11b supplies that law conditionally, for a uniform brane only.
  - The S11 record states that `c_L` is not a gravitational wave, so this entry is not about the carrier of
    gravity. (C6, C8.)

### Method for population passes

Method for a pass, per step record: read it for every statement of the form *this assumes*, *this rests
on*, *this is postulated at*, *this is deferred to*, *X enters at S**n***, and for every named retirement
condition. Each becomes an entry keyed by the step that must deliver. Where the record asserts something
about a step that has no record yet, that is a requirement by definition.

Two things to watch for, both seen already:
- A requirement can point **sideways**, not only backwards — S11's questions reduce to the S11b interface
  law, which is a sibling step, not a substrate one.
- The same object can be required by several sectors. Charge and magnetism ride the same brane–bulk
  coupling as light, so an entry may gain sources rather than being duplicated.

⭐⭐ **A SECOND ROUTE, added 2026-08-07 — ⛔ the method above would never have found `R-S8-04` or `R-S8-05`.**
Both came from asking, of a **known prior result our sector reproduces**, *why was it rejected in its own
time, and has that objection been answered here?* ⛔ Neither is anywhere in S9's or S10's records, because
the records only capture what their authors thought to doubt — and the sector reproduces MacCullagh's
algebra so cleanly that the objection to it never came up.

⇒ ⭐ **Run this route for every sector with identified prior art**, ⛔ not only the light sector.
⚠ It is the sharpest use of `CLAUDE.md` rule 16 available: the prior work's **failure modes** transfer as
obligations even where its **results** transfer as corroboration — and a result that matches prior art
tells you nothing about whether you inherited its problems.
⚠⚠ **The tell that this was overdue:** the closer a sector's agreement with prior art, the *less* anyone
thinks to ask what that prior art could not do. ⇒ ⛔ a clean reproduction is exactly when to run it.

**Honest sizing, now measured rather than guessed.** Pass 1 read two records and produced **seven**
entries, bringing the file from two entries to **nine total**, from a third of the sector. ⚠ That rate
is the argument for
running the pass **as each step closes**: reconstructing it at Phase 5, across five sectors, is precisely
where an implicit assumption goes missing.

⛔ **And pass 1 found no way to make this mechanical.** Every one of the seven came from reading prose for a
*flagged identification*, a *postulate with a live retirement condition*, or a *consequence stated about a
step that does not exist yet*. ⇒ ⛔ there is no grep for it, and a pass that produces entries quickly is a
pass that missed some.

## When this is done

Phase 5 knits the sectors and builds the substrate. At that point this file is the checklist the
substrate is tested against — the thing that answers *"is the brane–bulk we built sufficient to carry all
five forces"* by enumeration rather than by recollection.

## Why this exists

v3 is requirements-first: each sector states what it needs, and the knit happens last. The light sector
(S9, S10, S11, S11b) is built on **S1–S8, none of which have been run** — there are no step records for
them. That is the design, not an oversight: the substrate gets built once every sector has said what it
requires, so it can be checked against all of them at once rather than rebuilt per sector.

The bet only pays if the requirements are **captured**. Measured 2026-08-05: exactly two obligations are
recorded, both from S11, both about one quantity, both as inline anchors in a 1200-line plan. Everything
else a built sector assumes about the substrate is implicit prose spread across four step records.

`DEFECT_REGISTER.md` records what is *wrong*. `ANSATZ_LEDGER.md` records what is *postulated and not
derived*. Neither records **what a later step must deliver for an earlier result to stand.** That is this
file.

## The failure this prevents

At Phase 5 the sectors are knitted and the substrate is built against their combined requirements. If a
requirement was never written down, one of two things happens: the substrate is built without it and the
sector's result silently loses its footing, or it is rediscovered late and the substrate is rebuilt. Both
were survivable with one sector. With five they are not.

The S7 entry below is the shape of the problem. Standing at S7, the honest answer is "the slab width is
not selected" — a real result, bankable, and **insufficient**. Only S11 knows that the question must be
asked again with the width made position- and time-dependent. Nobody at S7 would think to ask.

## Entry schema

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | stable identifier, cited from both ends |
| `source` | the step that needs it |
| `target` | the step that must deliver it |
| `requirement` | **the object required**, named — not a derivation path for it |
| `on failure` | what breaks in the source step if the target cannot deliver |
| `status` | OPEN · DELIVERED · RETIRED (with the commit that changed it) |

Name the object; do not prescribe how the target should obtain it. A requirement that specifies a
derivation route manufactures arguments about the route — see `CLAUDE.md` rule 3.

Distinguish carefully:
- a **requirement** is an obligation on a *future* step;
- a **postulate** is a value or form assumed *here* and not derived — that belongs in `ANSATZ_LEDGER.md`;
- a **defect** is something already wrong — that belongs in `DEFECT_REGISTER.md`.

A postulate with a named retirement condition generates a requirement. `B_comp` below is exactly that.

### R-S8-01 — the form of the brane's quadratic stiffness functional

- **source** S9b (`steps/S9b_light_bending.md`, §§2/8, supplied transverse input only); S9, S10; S11 (`steps/S11_stray_longitudinal.md`, moves 2–3 / FORM control);

  substructure rather than chosen.
- **on failure** — this is the one input the light sector's central claim is **measurably** sensitive to,
  and S9's own controls prove it:
  - the gradient-elastic form `−½ μ_R Σ(∂_i u_j)²` — an ordinary elastic solid — carries **the same two
    transverse modes at the same `c² = μ_R/ρ_br`**, and *also* propagates the longitudinal;
  - the divergence-only form makes the roles **swap**: the transverse pair drops to `ω² = 0` and the
    longitudinal propagates.

  transverse ones.** If S8 delivers any other form, S9's and S10's transverse results may survive while
  the no-longitudinal claim — Maxwell's third demand, and the whole reason the sector exists — does not.

  Maxwell's no longitudinal mode"*. ⚠ That is a justification from the target, ⛔ not from the substrate.

  its magnitude**, as `DEFECT_REGISTER.md#B2` scopes it. ⛔ But it closes **one route**, and it says
  nothing about the **form**, so this requirement is live.
- **pass-2 consumers** — S11's unchanged transverse root rests on adding the trace invariant. As a
  first-route source only, its record says: *"The form control's `4/3` independently reproduces the
  corpus's rejected-Cauchy-branch coefficient"* (`steps/S11_stray_longitudinal.md:126–127`); the record

### R-S8-04 — what carries the brane's internal angular momentum

- **source** O2 (`steps/O2_steady_brane_balance.md`, register handoff); S9, S10, S11 · **target** S8 · **status** OPEN
- **requirement** — the object in the substructure that carries **internal angular momentum** on the brane,
  or the couple-stress it supports. ⛔ Not a mechanism, ⛔ not a model: the object, or a statement that there
  is none.
- **on failure** — ⛔⛔ **the curl-only stiffness functional is not an admissible continuum mechanics.** An
  energy in `(∇×u)²` alone has an **antisymmetric** Cauchy stress, and balance of angular momentum forces
  the Cauchy stress to be **symmetric** unless the medium carries distributed couples or internal spin. If
  the substructure supplies neither, the light sector's central form is inadmissible **regardless of its
  mode content** — S9's and S10's mode counts, dimensions and speeds would all be computed from a
  functional no medium can have.
- **note** — ⚠ **This is the objection that sank MacCullagh's aether**, and it is the one part of that
  theory the 19th century never answered: Stokes pressed it, and Kelvin's gyrostatic models were attempts to
  supply exactly this object. ⇒ ⭐ **prior art is the oracle here** — it tells us the obligation is real and
  that answers exist, ⛔ it tells us nothing about whether **ours** delivers one ⇒ `CLAUDE.md` rule 16.
  ⭐ Known families a delivered answer might fall into, ⛔ **none assumed and none prescribed**: continua
  with an independent microrotation degree of freedom (Cosserat/micropolar), and media with stored internal
  angular momentum.
  ⛔ **One family is the wrong one and should not be reached for:** modern *odd elasticity* buys an
  antisymmetric modulus tensor by making the solid **active and non-conservative**. MacCullagh's medium is
  **conservative** — it has a genuine energy functional — so a non-conservative realisation would be
  answering a different question.
  ⚠ `R-S8-01` asks for the **form** and is silent on admissibility; a substructure could deliver the
  curl-only form and still owe this.
- **O2 scope** — OPEN `𝒜_rot^live` carries this existing S8 obligation, including whether internal
  angular momentum/couple stress is present. O2 selects no stress symmetry or carrier and does not
  establish a curl-only live stress. The original conservative-MacCullagh objection keeps its
  original domain; it is not newly proved for an unspecified viscoelastic stress. The O2 addition
  carries the explicitly required carrier/admissibility question within its named material and
  corresponding power accounting; it adds no flowing constitutive response form. The accounting
  remains conditional with that question OPEN
  (`directives/O2_SHARED_PHYSICS.md`, §§3.2, 4, 6).

### R-S8-05 — the frame the brane's rotational stiffness is measured against

- **source** O2 (`steps/O2_steady_brane_balance.md`, register handoff); S9, S10, S11 · **target** S8 · **status** OPEN
- **requirement** — the frame with respect to which the brane's rotational stiffness is defined: **what
  `∇×u` is measured against.**
- **on failure** — for an infinitesimal rigid rotation `u = ω × r` the curl is `2ω ≠ 0`, so a curl-only
  energy is **nonzero when the whole medium is turned**. ⇒ if the reference is external, the medium knows
  an absolute orientation, and every result in the sector inherits a preferred-orientation signature that
  something later must hide. ⛔ That is a falsifiable consequence, ⛔ not a philosophical discomfort.
- **note** — ⭐ **A brane may escape this where a bulk aether cannot**, and the difference is the whole
  point of the entry. For a bulk medium *"rotation relative to what"* has no local answer — the 1839
  objection. For a **domain wall**, the wall supplies its own local frame (its normal, its induced
  geometry), rotation relative to the wall is meaningful and local, and rotating everything rotates the wall
  too ⇒ the stiffness would be **relative**, and the objection would not arise.
  ⚠⚠ **That is a HYPOTHESIS, ⛔ not a result.** Nothing in the corpus computes it. The slab-in-bulk
  calculation is where it is settled ⇒ **S11b-A** (interface response) is the existing partial artifact,
  built under the old pattern and on the rebuild list.
  ⚠ **A flowing medium does NOT answer this.** Flow bears on the **velocity** frame — whether a background
  drift is detectable — and the analog-gravity route hides it in an effective metric. ⛔ Orientation is a
  **separate** objection: being carried is not being turned. ⇒ ⭐ do not let one argument discharge both.
- **O2 scope** — OPEN `𝒜_rot^live` retains the physical rotational frame as an existing S8
  obligation explicitly carried by the spec. Neither radial flow, the graph normal nor LAB_HELD
  chooses that material frame. O2's named force/power accounting retains the frame question OPEN;
  this addition supplies no frame or new rotational-response form. O2 does not extend the original
  curl-only objection to an unspecified live stress
  (`directives/O2_SHARED_PHYSICS.md`, §§1, 3.2, 6, 7).

### R-S22-01 — how the energy a throat releases splits among light, the extra wave and the bulk

- **source**
  - S11 (`steps/S11_stray_longitudinal.md`, departure table and the paragraphs after it). The table gives the
    question "whether matter directly observes the second cone" the owner "derived matter/interface
    coupling". The record says "A second cone is only a departure if matter COUPLES to it", and describes
    matter as "a throat held open by a trapped brane-shear standing wave".
  - The photon survey, E32–E34 and E38 (`PHOTON_POLARIZATION_SURVEY.md` §4). Each is "In apparent conflict",
    under conditions that differ by entry. In the survey's words, the classification rests on "E32–E34 on
    matter coupling and, for the blackbody comparison, ordinary thermal-radiation participation; E38
    additionally on the extra branch's cosmological relativistic population, energy/perturbation mapping and
    decoupling history". (C6, C7.)
- **target** S22 (the nonlinear throat solve), together with Q2 (the mouth source and its held datum) and
  S12 (the throat's order-conversion source and its boundary data). These owners were chosen by the user on
  2026-10-19; the S11 record itself names only "derived matter/interface coupling". (C8.)
  The user's 2026-10-20 **"Keep S12"** decision retains every owner. S12 stays OPEN for its
  forms, delivered only after the brane is defined following the force sectors; this requirements
  record delivers none of those forms (S12 record §§5–7, retrieval M18).
- **status** OPEN
- **requirement** — Consider a throat held open by its trapped shear wave. The trapped-wave state can change,
  the throat can move, and its mouth can change shape. When any of these happens, the object is the energy
  released, with its frequency content and rate, and how it splits among three channels:
  - the free transverse waves (light);
  - the extra longitudinal wave (S11's second cone);
  - the bulk.

  The entry also requires the reverse: how much of the energy each channel carries in is taken up by a
  throat, at each frequency.
- **on failure** — S11's departure cannot be classified. The record makes the second cone a departure only
  if matter couples to it, and without these objects nothing decides whether matter observes it. E32–E34
  and E38 stay "in apparent conflict", with their condition undecided.
- **note: what a delivered split would and would not decide** —
  - **Each measurement has its own conditions** (survey §4):
    - **E33**, the laboratory blackbody, needs the extra wave to be an additional ordinary thermal mode,
      with the usual occupation, energy and dispersion, and a calibrated emission and absorption response.
    - **E34**, the CMB spectrum, needs its power to enter the calibrated CMB radiance rather than cancel in
      the sky/reference comparison.
    - **E38**, `N_eff`, needs it to be extra gravitating radiation, populated and relativistic in the early
      universe. The survey adds that a weak population or earlier decoupling is not generically excluded.
  - **The split alone decides none of them.** Whether the extra wave is populated depends on several things:
    - its emission and uptake rates, compared with each measurement's timescale;
    - its escape into the bulk;
    - its initial population and the expansion history.

    What a populated wave then carries depends on its own speed. In S11 that speed is set by `B_comp/ρ_br`
    (`R-S6-01`), not by light's `μ_R/ρ_br`. So a share comparable to light's is not by itself a conflict,
    and neither is equilibrium with matter. Nor does a small share by itself rule one out.
  - **The falsifier** is each measurement, applied under its own conditions to the population and power
    that these objects, the extra wave's speed and its escape into the bulk predict. That application is
    later work. This entry states no bound; compare the note in `R-S12-01`.
  - **The quantum part.** The survey's conditions also assume the usual quantum occupation. The plan
    assigns that to a separate project (`V3_STEP_PLAN.md:1198–1204`; survey [P8]), so a classical split
    does not settle that part. (C7.)
- **relation** —
  - S22's linear test 1 asks how much light passing a supplied defect profile converts into the
    longitudinal mode. S11c asked how much light converts where the brane changes (`V3_STEP_PLAN.md:508`).
    Both concern incoming light; neither is a throat's own emission.
  - S22's linear test 2 asks whether the longitudinal mode radiates into the bulk, and needs the interface
    law (`V3_STEP_PLAN.md:1181`). That escape enters the extra wave's population. So applying any
    measurement under this entry also needs test 2's result.
  - The S11 record adds that at homogeneous linear order "the mode's bulk leakage and direct observability
    require the brane–bulk interface law". S11b supplies that law conditionally, for a uniform brane only.
  - The S11 record states that `c_L` is not a gravitational wave, so this entry is not about the carrier of
    gravity. (C6, C8.)

### Method for population passes

Method for a pass, per step record: read it for every statement of the form *this assumes*, *this rests
on*, *this is postulated at*, *this is deferred to*, *X enters at S**n***, and for every named retirement
condition. Each becomes an entry keyed by the step that must deliver. Where the record asserts something
about a step that has no record yet, that is a requirement by definition.

Two things to watch for, both seen already:
- A requirement can point **sideways**, not only backwards — S11's questions reduce to the S11b interface
  law, which is a sibling step, not a substrate one.
- The same object can be required by several sectors. Charge and magnetism ride the same brane–bulk
  coupling as light, so an entry may gain sources rather than being duplicated.

⭐⭐ **A SECOND ROUTE, added 2026-08-07 — ⛔ the method above would never have found `R-S8-04` or `R-S8-05`.**
Both came from asking, of a **known prior result our sector reproduces**, *why was it rejected in its own
time, and has that objection been answered here?* ⛔ Neither is anywhere in S9's or S10's records, because
the records only capture what their authors thought to doubt — and the sector reproduces MacCullagh's
algebra so cleanly that the objection to it never came up.

⇒ ⭐ **Run this route for every sector with identified prior art**, ⛔ not only the light sector.
⚠ It is the sharpest use of `CLAUDE.md` rule 16 available: the prior work's **failure modes** transfer as
obligations even where its **results** transfer as corroboration — and a result that matches prior art
tells you nothing about whether you inherited its problems.
⚠⚠ **The tell that this was overdue:** the closer a sector's agreement with prior art, the *less* anyone
thinks to ask what that prior art could not do. ⇒ ⛔ a clean reproduction is exactly when to run it.

**Honest sizing, now measured rather than guessed.** Pass 1 read two records and produced **seven**
entries, bringing the file from two entries to **nine total**, from a third of the sector. ⚠ That rate
is the argument for
running the pass **as each step closes**: reconstructing it at Phase 5, across five sectors, is precisely
where an implicit assumption goes missing.

⛔ **And pass 1 found no way to make this mechanical.** Every one of the seven came from reading prose for a
*flagged identification*, a *postulate with a live retirement condition*, or a *consequence stated about a
step that does not exist yet*. ⇒ ⛔ there is no grep for it, and a pass that produces entries quickly is a
pass that missed some.

## When this is done

Phase 5 knits the sectors and builds the substrate. At that point this file is the checklist the
substrate is tested against — the thing that answers *"is the brane–bulk we built sufficient to carry all
five forces"* by enumeration rather than by recollection.

45: ## Why this exists
46: 
47: v3 is requirements-first: each sector states what it needs, and the knit happens last. The light sector
48: (S9, S10, S11, S11b) is built on **S1–S8, none of which have been run** — there are no step records for
49: them. That is the design, not an oversight: the substrate gets built once every sector has said what it
50: requires, so it can be checked against all of them at once rather than rebuilt per sector.
51: 
52: The bet only pays if the requirements are **captured**. Measured 2026-08-05: exactly two obligations are
53: recorded, both from S11, both about one quantity, both as inline anchors in a 1200-line plan. Everything
54: else a built sector assumes about the substrate is implicit prose spread across four step records.
55: 
56: `DEFECT_REGISTER.md` records what is *wrong*. `ANSATZ_LEDGER.md` records what is *postulated and not
57: derived*. Neither records **what a later step must deliver for an earlier result to stand.** That is this
58: file.
59: 
60: ## The failure this prevents
61: 
62: At Phase 5 the sectors are knitted and the substrate is built against their combined requirements. If a
63: requirement was never written down, one of two things happens: the substrate is built without it and the
64: sector's result silently loses its footing, or it is rediscovered late and the substrate is rebuilt. Both
65: were survivable with one sector. With five they are not.
66: 
67: The S7 entry below is the shape of the problem. Standing at S7, the honest answer is "the slab width is
68: not selected" — a real result, bankable, and **insufficient**. Only S11 knows that the question must be
69: asked again with the width made position- and time-dependent. Nobody at S7 would think to ask.
70: 
71: ## Entry schema
72: 
73: | field | meaning |
74: |---|---|
75: | `id` | stable identifier, cited from both ends |
76: | `source` | the step that needs it |
77: | `target` | the step that must deliver it |
78: | `requirement` | **the object required**, named — not a derivation path for it |
79: | `on failure` | what breaks in the source step if the target cannot deliver |
80: | `status` | OPEN · DELIVERED · RETIRED (with the commit that changed it) |
81: 
82: Name the object; do not prescribe how the target should obtain it. A requirement that specifies a
83: derivation route manufactures arguments about the route — see `CLAUDE.md` rule 3.
84: 
85: Distinguish carefully:
86: - a **requirement** is an obligation on a *future* step;
87: - a **postulate** is a value or form assumed *here* and not derived — that belongs in `ANSATZ_LEDGER.md`;
88: - a **defect** is something already wrong — that belongs in `DEFECT_REGISTER.md`.
89: 
90: A postulate with a named retirement condition generates a requirement. `B_comp` below is exactly that.
91: 
92: ---

465: ### R-S8-04 — what carries the brane's internal angular momentum
466: 
467: - **source** O2 (`steps/O2_steady_brane_balance.md`, register handoff); S9, S10, S11 · **target** S8 · **status** OPEN
468: - **requirement** — the object in the substructure that carries **internal angular momentum** on the brane,
469:   or the couple-stress it supports. ⛔ Not a mechanism, ⛔ not a model: the object, or a statement that there
470:   is none.
471: - **on failure** — ⛔⛔ **the curl-only stiffness functional is not an admissible continuum mechanics.** An
472:   energy in `(∇×u)²` alone has an **antisymmetric** Cauchy stress, and balance of angular momentum forces
473:   the Cauchy stress to be **symmetric** unless the medium carries distributed couples or internal spin. If
474:   the substructure supplies neither, the light sector's central form is inadmissible **regardless of its
475:   mode content** — S9's and S10's mode counts, dimensions and speeds would all be computed from a
476:   functional no medium can have.
477: - **note** — ⚠ **This is the objection that sank MacCullagh's aether**, and it is the one part of that
478:   theory the 19th century never answered: Stokes pressed it, and Kelvin's gyrostatic models were attempts to
479:   supply exactly this object. ⇒ ⭐ **prior art is the oracle here** — it tells us the obligation is real and
480:   that answers exist, ⛔ it tells us nothing about whether **ours** delivers one ⇒ `CLAUDE.md` rule 16.
481:   ⭐ Known families a delivered answer might fall into, ⛔ **none assumed and none prescribed**: continua
482:   with an independent microrotation degree of freedom (Cosserat/micropolar), and media with stored internal
483:   angular momentum.
484:   ⛔ **One family is the wrong one and should not be reached for:** modern *odd elasticity* buys an
485:   antisymmetric modulus tensor by making the solid **active and non-conservative**. MacCullagh's medium is
486:   **conservative** — it has a genuine energy functional — so a non-conservative realisation would be
487:   answering a different question.
488:   ⚠ `R-S8-01` asks for the **form** and is silent on admissibility; a substructure could deliver the
489:   curl-only form and still owe this.
490: - **O2 scope** — OPEN `𝒜_rot^live` carries this existing S8 obligation, including whether internal
491:   angular momentum/couple stress is present. O2 selects no stress symmetry or carrier and does not
492:   establish a curl-only live stress. The original conservative-MacCullagh objection keeps its
493:   original domain; it is not newly proved for an unspecified viscoelastic stress. The O2 addition
494:   carries the explicitly required carrier/admissibility question within its named material and
495:   corresponding power accounting; it adds no flowing constitutive response form. The accounting
496:   remains conditional with that question OPEN
497:   (`directives/O2_SHARED_PHYSICS.md`, §§3.2, 4, 6).

499: ### R-S8-05 — the frame the brane's rotational stiffness is measured against

504: - **on failure** — for an infinitesimal rigid rotation `u = ω × r` the curl is `2ω ≠ 0`, so a curl-only
505:   energy is **nonzero when the whole medium is turned**. ⇒ if the reference is external, the medium knows

510:   objection. For a **domain wall**, the wall supplies its own local frame (its normal, its induced

791: **Counting the two observables under item 5.** The rule is “It counts the deflection
792: and the radar slope as separate tests only where the printed objects show their conditions differ.”
793: M17 retrieves that rule and both engines' complete γ objects, including their attached gates,
794: for general B, R_FLOW_ONLY, R_SPEED_ONLY, R_TILT_ONLY and conditional F_FLOW/F_LIVE.
795: On each object's on-domain `GM≠0` stratum, PY's γ-difference solution set is `{0}` and WL's
796: relation contains `gammaDifference==0 && GM!=0`. Thus the two observables are **not counted
797: as separate tests at these selected grades on that stratum**, in either engine. This is a
798: count of the printed reference-comparison constraints, not a claim of cross-engine equivalence
799: or observational redundancy outside this model point. (M17; paired conditions M13.)

801: At `GM=0`, PY separately prints the full real interval when both observable compatibility
802: functionals vanish, and `EmptySet` on the other three printed vanishing/nonvanishing combinations.
803: WL prints `GM==0` with both functionals zero, without a constraint on `gammaDifference`, and
804: no further compatible alternative. Each engine's individual γ objects retain the corresponding
805: unconstrained/empty singular strata. The record does not replace these by γ-difference zero:
806: γ is unidentifiable on the compatible singular stratum, and the incompatible strata supply no
807: joint γ solution. These strata establish no additional separate γ test under item 5; two
808: independent tests are not counted from the unrestricted difference. Outside the respective gates,
809: the objects are `NOT_ESTABLISHED`. (M17.)

813: does not put the above counting decision on hold. Nor are the differing strings treated as a

815: Part C/bulk-only condition rewrites retain M13's field distinctions and earn no additional
